newsitem.title: INDIA: India says to announce new power policy soon.
newsitem.headline: India says to announce new power policy soon.

text.p: India will announce a new power policy which would address all problems of the sector, Power Minister Y.K. Alagh said on Wednesday.

A government statement quoted Alagh as saying that the projected capacity addition as assessed for the ninth plan (1992-1997) might fall short of the actual, needing to double efforts to maximise capacity addition during the plan period.
He said that the new policy would be announced after the monsoon session of Parliament, which is scheduled to start in the third week of July and would continue until mid-August.
The policy will encompass all aspects of the power sector, including generation, transmission and distribution.

Alagh said there was scope for improvement in the average plant load factor of thermal power plants. He said there was a need for higher investment in transmission and distribution to transfer power from surplus to deficit regions.
The minister was addressing a meeting of parliamentary deputies on the performance of the state-run Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCI).
He said that PGCI, the state-owned national grid, would play a major role in the exchange of power between India and its neighbours such as Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal.
The statement said that PGCI made a profit of three billion rupees on sales of 10 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March). It did not give comparative figures for the previous year.
